Subject: POC Trial Workload Intake - AcmeHealth (follow-up)

Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. Quick recap and next steps to get the POC scoped and scheduled:

Summary from call:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Acme Health triage assistant (PHI-handling via Private deployment) and measure latency/cost for ~2 week evaluation.
- Primary success criteria discussed: model accuracy on clinical triage prompts, p95 latency under 250ms for synthetic test harness, error rate <0.5%, and cost target under $0.015/token (team to confirm budget).

What we need from you (workload / traffic intake):
1) Expected steady-state RPS and peak burst RPS (typical duration of burst)
2) Typical prompt token length and expected completion token length (averages + 95th pct)
3) Expected concurrency (simultaneous sessions) and percent of requests that are multi-turn chat vs single-turn
4) Any traffic patterns (time-of-day, weekday/weekend peaks) and sample traces (CSV is fine)
5) Any integration constraints: strict IP allowlisting, proxy, private endpoints, or sample test credentials we should use

Attached are two helpful templates: poc_mop_template.xlsx (success criteria & ownership template) and traffic_profile_sample.csv. If you can fill those and return by Friday (Apr 9) we can lock dates.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Intake review & infra sync (Ben) — propose Thu Apr 8, 10:00 AM PT
- Kickoff + provisioning — Mon Apr 12
- 2-week trial window Apr 12–26 with mid-trial check on Apr 19

Ownership: Marissa (trial plan / success criteria), Ben (infra / provisioning), Acme — technical lead: Samantha.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call to walk through the templates.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes and templates. Quick answers below and I've attached a short sample export (acme_traffic_sample.csv) with anonymized request/timestamp/token columns.

Workload profile (current best estimates):
- Steady-state RPS: 5-10 requests/sec (these are user-initiated triage requests)
- Peak bursts: up to ~70-80 RPS for short spikes (5-10 seconds) during system syncs or morning batch events
- Prompt tokens: avg 40 tokens, 95th pct 120 tokens
- Completion tokens: avg 180 tokens, 95th pct 420 tokens
- Concurrency: expect ~15-25 simultaneous active sessions during peak; about 20 is our planning number
- Chat vs single-turn: roughly 60% multi-turn conversations (3-4 turns on avg), 40% single-turn
- Traffic patterns: weekday mornings 8-10am local see ~35% of daily volume; lighter weekends

Compliance/infra notes: We will require a private deployment (VPC) or Private control plane with traffic routed over our VPN. We cannot share real PHI — will provide anonymized samples.

Timeline: the team is good with your proposed kickoff Apr 12. We should be able to turn around the filled intake template by Apr 9.

Attaching: acme_traffic_sample.csv (anonymized).

Let me know if you want any additional telemetry fields (e.g., response size, upstream latencies).

Thanks,
Samantha
Senior Engineering Manager
Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: POC Trial Workload Intake - AcmeHealth (follow-up)

Samantha —

Perfect, this is exactly what we needed. A few follow-ups / clarifications to make sure we size and configure the trial correctly:

1) Multi-turn behavior: when you say ~60% multi-turn, is the majority of those conversations short (3 turns) or do you have a long-tail of 10+ turns for some users? That affects KV cache sizing and memory.
2) Bursts: are the 70-80 RPS bursts happening predictably (scheduled sync) or are they organic (user-driven)? If scheduled, what times?
3) Success criteria: can you confirm the priority order — is accuracy > latency, or do you want latency as hard SLO? We'll propose: accuracy (pass rate on your clinical prompt set) as primary, with p95 latency <= 250ms as required for the UI.
4) Cost guardrails: do you have a token-spend monthly or per-trial budget we should watch against? If not, we can set a temporary alert threshold.

Proposed evaluation plan (we will add to the MOP):
- Pre-trial: run a synthetic replay using your sample to validate p95 latency and tail behavior (Marissa/Ben)
- Trial: route a percent of traffic (or replay) through Redwood Private endpoints; run model/quantization variants if needed
- Metrics: accuracy on shared eval prompts, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token consumption and estimated $/token spend
- Acceptance: agreed pass rate on eval set + no critical infra issues for 48h

Next steps:
- Ben, can you join Thu Apr 8 10:00 AM PT for the infra intake?
- Samantha / Raj: please add the filled poc_mop_template.xlsx and any additional traces to the Drive folder linked above.

Thanks — I will update the HubSpot deal with the intake details after the call.

- Provisioning: for the expected peak (~80 RPS with 20 concurrency and avg 220 tokens per request including completion), we can start with a 2-GPU dedicated pool (A100-class) with autoscaling allowed to burst one additional node for spikes. If you prefer a conservative approach we can run the synthetic replay first and then scale to a larger pool.
- KV cache: if you have long multi-turn sessions (10+ turns) we should increase KV cache limits; otherwise defaults should be fine.
- Private networking: Samantha, please share the allowlist CIDRs or the VPN handoff details before Apr 12 so we can pre-configure.
- Test creds: we recommend a short-lived test API key (no PHI) or a replay bundle; do not send any real PHI.

I can also prepare a short runbook for the trial provisioning prior to the call.
